title: 09 · Bento grid · Holdfast
strengths: Every tile is working product with data that ties together: ticket #48207 is the selected inbox row, the SLA clock ('14:32', 'Enterprise · 1 h first reply') and the snooze menu's subject

A real tile hierarchy: one 5x2 inbox, a sun-yellow SLA tile, an ink keyboard tile and two white tiles, one gap (16 px) and one radius (24 px); colour does one job each (yellow = time running, ink = keys)
One grotesk (Schibsted Grotesk) carries it by size and weight: 'Inbox.' in 600 then the sentence in 400; the headline is regular with no highlighted phrase
The macro card bleeds off its tile's edge, breaking the box-in-box rhythm the way shipped bentos do
slop_signals: A generic SaaS headline ('Built around the promises you make customers.') over a structure that Plain and incident.io already ship
The Satisfaction tile has a dead band above its figure
Invented data reused across pieces: 'used 312 times' repeats the 312 from styles/08, and customer names echo other pieces (Quarry, Kettle)
fixes: Give the headline a fact (a breach rate, a time) instead of a promise
Tighten the Satisfaction tile so the chart and figure fill it
Rename 'Quarry & Vale' and 'Kettle Robotics', and change the 312

references.what: Support feature tiles including an SLA 'First response time' control
Six feature tiles, each holding a real fragment of the product
A macro with a 'First name' token shown inside the product

facts: Name and number reuse: 'Quarry' is the brand of app-screens/09 and appears in product/01 ('Quarry Lane Books'); 'Kettle' appears in heroes/11 ('Kettle & Co.'); '312' is also styles/08's connector count
